boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Deep Bottom I record (July 27-29, 1864) in the Richmond-Petersburg Campaign [June 1864-March 1865]. The Crater (VA070) follows on July 30. Army-wide returns, raid-wide and multi-action loss totals, and the siege as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 'Corps' and the live field zero. Hancock names Gibbon's, Barlow's and Mott's divisions with Sheridan's cavalry, adds Birge's brigade of a little over 2,500, and relays Grant's information of seven enemy brigades and a little cavalry in his front. Humphreys says Wilcox's and Kershaw's divisions held the line, Heth's joined on the 27th, and Field's and Fitzhugh Lee's divisions on the 29th.
claims.rationale: Formation lists and one brigade figure; no return for either force. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Hancock says he decided, with Sheridan and Meade's approval, to cross at the lower bridge and turn the position, and that Grant did not want the works assaulted; Humphreys credits Sheridan's dismounted troopers with repulsing Kershaw's attack. The frozen commanders are Major General Hancock (US) and Major General Field (CS); the live page matches.
claims.rationale: Direction attributed as stated; Field's role is not described in the inspected passages. No listed commander receives automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory; NPS says the Union turning efforts were abandoned when the Confederates reinforced and counterattacked. Hancock reports four 20-pounder Parrotts taken on the 27th and nearly 200 prisoners on the 28th; Humphreys says the expedition reduced the Petersburg garrison to three infantry divisions and drew two of three cavalry divisions north.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The diversion's effect on July 30 is campaign contribution, not this record's result.

open_questions: Sheridan's, Barlow's and Miles's reports (Nos. 20-21), Foster's report, Field's and Kershaw's reports, the Second Corps casualty list (blank in OCR) and Sheridan's 1866 report passage (Volume XXXVI; not re-selected) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, later commander of its Second Corps, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; it relies on Meade's, Hancock's, Warren's, Burnside's, Parke's and Wilson's reports and quotes Lee's, Beauregard's and Gordon's despatches, so it is not independent of those families. Gillmore's, Meade's, Hancock's, Burnside's, Wilson's, Hampton's, Stannard's and Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volumes XXXVI (Part 2), XL, XLII and XLVI (Part 1), are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; each volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Lee's telegrams largely relay subordinates' reports. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
